short: ISO 45001 is the ISO requirements standard for an occupational health and safety management system; the current edition is ISO 45001:2018 with Amendment 1:2024, a revision is at Draft International Standard stage, and it is held as a certificate issued by a certification body.
title: ISO 45001, Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems
subtitle: The ISO requirements standard for managing workplace health and safety
body_html:
What ISO 45001 is

ISO 45001 sets the requirements for an occupational health and safety (OH&S) management system, with guidance for its use. Its purpose, in ISO's summary, is to let organizations provide safe and healthy workplaces by preventing work-related injury and ill health and by improving OH&S performance. It is written by ISO/TC 283. The current edition, the first, was published on 12 March 2018 and amended on 23 February 2024. ISO Open Data shows its revision at Draft International Standard stage.

What it covers

  • Eliminating hazards and minimising OH&S risks, including weaknesses in the system itself.
  • Meeting legal and other requirements.
  • Setting and achieving OH&S objectives, and continual improvement of OH&S performance.
  • Taking account of workers and other interested parties.

How conformity is shown

ISO publishes the standard and sells its text. ISO Open Data, the dataset ISO publishes for reuse, records the edition, the committee and the scope, and that is what this page is built from. It does not record who holds a certificate. A certificate against a requirements standard like this one is issued by a certification body after an audit, and it names that body, the edition, the scope and the dates.

What a claim does not mean

ISO says the standard sets no OH&S performance criteria and does not prescribe how the system must be designed. It does not cover product safety, property damage or environmental impacts beyond the risks to workers and others concerned. A claim of conformity is only acceptable if every requirement is met without exclusion.

ISO 45001 in data centers

Data center work carries high-voltage electrical work, battery rooms, fire suppression gases, heavy equipment and contractors on site. An ISO 45001 certificate shows the operator manages those risks to people under an audited system at the sites named. It says nothing about the security or availability of customer equipment.

  • Scope. A certificate covers named sites, services or activities. One site certified does not mean every site the operator runs is certified.
  • Edition. The certificate names the edition it was audited against.
  • Certification body and certificate number. These let a reader confirm the certificate with the body that issued it.
  • Dates. A certificate has an issue date and an expiry date.

Related standards

See also ISO 14001, often certified together with it, and the Standards and Frameworks hub.

Primary sources

  • ISO 45001:2018, ISO standard page (linked for readers; iso.org refuses automated readers, so the facts above come from ISO Open Data)
  • ISO 45001:2018/Amd 1:2024
  • ISO Open Data, deliverables metadata: edition, publication date, committee and scope
